location.basis: Centre of the fenced archaeological mound read on the imagery at about 27.3484 N, 68.7045 E, at the foot of the hill carrying the 18th-century Talpur fort; the published Wikipedia position for Kot Diji is 27.34556 N, 68.70667 E, about 350 m to the south-east on the fort hill.

main_system_reason: No system: we found no measurable Harappan line.
notes: The Esri imagery here is a Vantor Vivid Advanced mosaic from a GeoEye-1 scene of 15 January 2024 (source resolution 0.46 m), which the service also serves at zoom 19; we looked at both zoom 18 and zoom 19. The Harappan and Early Harappan mound lies inside a modern polygonal boundary wall west of the road. Its surface is cut by old trenches and erosion gullies, with short wall stubs visible in places, but no wall, street or fortification face runs straight for 20 m. The large fort on the hill to the south-east is Talpur-period and was not considered. Kot Diji is not measurable from this imagery.
